headline: Sean Parker is rebuilding Stability AI around music with $76M from Sony, Warner, and Universal
summary: Napster co-founder Sean Parker returns to music, leading Stability AI's pivot into AI music tools, backed by $76 million and catalog licenses from major labels like Sony and Universal.
details: Napster co-founder Sean Parker has re-entered the music industry, aiming to transform Stability AI. He joined the image-generator startup two years ago during its $80 million rescue after founder Emad Mostaque's ouster. Parker states he is "playing by the rules this time."

Parker's vision is to establish Stability AI as the leading AI toolmaker for music professionals. This strategic pivot marks a significant shift for the company, moving beyond its initial focus on image generation.

To support this new direction, Stability AI secured $76 million in funding in late August. This investment came from major industry players including Sony, Warner, and Universal, who also licensed their music catalogs for training purposes.

Following the funding, Stability AI has already released three new audio models and AI music-editing software. These tools can generate full instrumental tracks or short snippets from text prompts, offering new creative possibilities for artists.

An upcoming update promises even more intuitive control, allowing users to hum a melody or beatbox a drum pattern to guide the AI's generation. This feature aims to make AI music creation more accessible and interactive for professionals.

headline: Apple confirms iPhone 18 Pro Max AT&T cellular issues, requires hardware replacement
summary: A 'small number' of iPhone 18 Pro Max devices on AT&T are losing cellular service, and Apple states these units require a hardware replacement to fix the issue.
details: Apple has confirmed an issue causing a 'small number' of iPhone 18 Pro Max devices on AT&T to lose cellular service. Affected units will require a hardware replacement to resolve the problem.

The specific technical cause for this cellular connectivity failure has not been publicly disclosed by Apple. Users experiencing these symptoms are advised to contact Apple Support or visit an authorized service provider for diagnosis and repair.
